prediction.likelyOutcome: Most likely a split decision: the landlord establishes some tenant breach (the tenants vacated and never paid anything), but recovers only a fraction of the $302,896 sought — Carroll's own emails deferring rent until the bathrooms and power panel were finished badly undercut the back-rent claim, and the $107,781.91 in landlord's-work costs is largely the landlord's own contractual and code obligation with the quasi-contract counts already dismissed. The tenants' counterclaim likely succeeds at most in part (HVAC/thermostat), and is unquantified, so its main effect is defensive rather than as an affirmative recovery.

issues.label: Back Rent ($45,736.45) vs. the Email Rent Deferral
Tenants' Counterclaim — HVAC and Bathroom Delivery
Personal Guaranties of McKinney and Saul
Dismissal of Unjust Enrichment and Promissory Estoppel

outcome.description: After a bench trial the circuit court found the lease effective date was modified to May 1, 2022, that the landlord did not breach and the tenants did, and entered judgment against the tenants and guarantors jointly and severally for $51,336.45 (back rent of $45,736.45 plus $5,600 demolition costs, each equal to the component the landlord requested), declining the $107,781.91 landlord's-work and $143,777.60 reletting-cost claims; no attorney's fees are mentioned. The court of appeals affirmed the judgment on direct appeal and, on cross-appeal, reversed the denial of reletting costs and remanded for findings on whether the $143,777.60 qualifies as reasonable reletting costs under the lease.
